docs.title: How to Run the Model for the First Time
docs.text: This section provides a quick-start procedure for running CE-QUAL-W2 using one of the included example applications. The DeGray Reservoir example, which includes sediment diagenesis, is used here to demonstrate the basic workflow. For instructions on setting up a new model application from scratch, see How to Set Up and Run a Model Application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Running CE-QUAL-W2 involves four steps:

  1. Copy the model executables into the example directory.
  2. Run the preprocessor to validate input files.
  3. Run the model to produce simulation output.
  4. Evaluate the output files to verify correct model behavior.

docs.title: Step 1: Copy Executables to the Example Directory
docs.text:
The CE-QUAL-W2 distribution includes pre-compiled executables and a set of example applications. To get started, copy the following executables into the example directory:

  • Copy the model executable (e.g., w2_v4_64.exe) from the executables/w2 directory.
  • Copy the preprocessor executable (e.g., preW2-v4_64.exe) from the executables/w2 preprocessor directory.

Place both files into the example directory examples/DeGray Reservoir with sediment diagenesis.

The figure below shows the contents of the DeGray Reservoir example directory before copying the executables. The directory contains the control file, bathymetry file, meteorological input files, and other required input files.

docs.title: Step 2: Run the Preprocessor
docs.text:
The preprocessor reads the control file and all associated input files, checks for errors, and reports any warnings or problems before the full simulation is run.

  1. Double-click preW2-v4_64.exe to launch the preprocessor.

  2. The preprocessor produces three output files:

    File Description pre.opt Preprocessor output summary pre.wrn Warning messages pre.err Error messages

  3. Open pre.err and verify that no errors are reported.

Check both warnings and errors

Always review pre.wrn in addition to pre.err. Warnings may indicate input values that are technically valid but physically unrealistic, such as unusually large Manning's friction coefficients or mismatched segment lengths. Addressing warnings before running the model can save significant troubleshooting time.

Resolve all errors before proceeding

If pre.err contains error messages, correct the corresponding input files and rerun the preprocessor. Do not proceed to running the model until the preprocessor reports no errors.

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Model
docs.text:
Once the preprocessor completes without errors, run the full simulation.

  1. Double-click w2_v4_64.exe to launch the model.
  2. A dialog box appears showing simulation progress, including the current simulation day and elapsed run time.
  3. When the simulation finishes, the model produces output files in the same directory.

docs.title: Step 4: Evaluate Output
docs.text:
After the simulation completes, review the output files to verify that the model ran correctly. The primary output file for initial review is snp.opt, which contains snapshot output of water surface elevations, velocities, temperatures, and constituent concentrations at user-specified intervals.

Use snp.opt and other output files for post-processing, visualization, and comparison with observed data. For details on output file formats, see the output files documentation.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: For a detailed guide on setting up a new CE-QUAL-W2 application, including grid development, boundary condition specification, and calibration procedures, see How to Set Up and Run a Model Application.

docs.title: How to Set Up and Run a Model Application
docs.text: This section describes the complete workflow for setting up and running a new CE-QUAL-W2 model application. The procedure consists of seven steps, from constructing boundary condition files through evaluating model output. For a quick-start guide using an included example application, see How to Run the Model for the First Time.

docs.title: Workflow Overview
docs.text:
1. Construct all boundary condition files
  2. Develop the model grid
  3. Edit the main control file
  4. Edit auxiliary input files
  5. Run the preprocessor
  6. Run the W2 model
  7. Evaluate output files

docs.title: Step 1: Construct All Boundary Condition Files
docs.text:
Boundary condition files provide the external forcing data that drive the model simulation. These files include:

  • Flow rates, temperatures, and concentrations for all inflows
  • Meteorological conditions for each waterbody
  • Water levels for head boundary conditions
  • Shading coefficients for each segment
  • Wind sheltering coefficients for segments
  • Outflow rates and withdrawal rates
  • Precipitation files

All boundary condition files can be developed in a spreadsheet application such as Microsoft Excel. Input files may have either a Comma-Separated Values (CSV, .csv) or fixed-format text (.npt) extension. The file name and file type for most input files can be specified by the user in the control file.

docs.title: File Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Inflow files typically use the following prefixes:

Prefix Content q Flow rate t Temperature c Concentration

The meteorological file is commonly named met*.npt or met*.csv.

docs.title: Creating Input Files in Excel
docs.text:
The following procedure demonstrates how to create a flow input file for the model.

  1. Open a new Excel worksheet.
  2. Enter a descriptive comment on the first line (e.g., "Inflow #1 2003"). The first three lines are ignored by the model and are used for descriptors and column headers.
  3. Skip a line or row.
  4. On row 3, add column headers: first column JDAY, second column Q(m³/s).
  5. On row 4, enter a Julian day value (e.g., 1.5 corresponds to January 1 at 12 noon) and a corresponding flow value (e.g., 10.0, entered as a decimal).
  6. On row 5, enter the final Julian day (e.g., 365) and corresponding flow value (e.g., 15).

The model can linearly interpolate between data points or treat the values as step functions.

docs.title: Saving Input Files
docs.text:
There are two approaches for saving input files in a format compatible with CE-QUAL-W2:

  • Fixed-format text (.npt): Select all cells in the worksheet and set all column widths to 8 characters. Use File > Save As, choose the .prn format, and enter the desired filename in quotes (e.g., "qin_branch1.npt").
  • CSV format (.csv): Save the file directly as a CSV from Excel, or use the Excel macro utility w2_tools_L.xlam (available from the Portland State University (PSU) CE-QUAL-W2 website) to write the file in CSV format. See the W2 Tools Excel Macro Utility User Manual for details.

CSV file header requirement

The first character in line 1 of a CSV input file must be a dollar sign ($).

docs.title: Julian Day Conversion
docs.text:
CE-QUAL-W2 uses Julian days for all time references in calculations and boundary conditions. To convert a calendar date to a Julian day in Excel, use the following formula:

=<Cell with Date> - DATEVALUE("1/1/XXXX") + 1

Replace XXXX with the reference year for the start of Julian days. Convert the cell format to a number after applying the formula.

Tip

A full description of all model input file formats is provided in Part 3 of this manual.

docs.title: Step 2: Develop the Model Grid
docs.text: The model grid is defined by a bathymetry file for each waterbody. For the DeGray Reservoir example, this file is named bth1.csv. An example of the bathymetry file format for a reservoir is provided in Part 3 of this manual.

docs.title: Bathymetry File Development Procedure
docs.text:
1. Obtain x,y,z topographic data for the waterbody.
  2. For reservoirs or rivers, merge the topographic data with digital elevation model (DEM) data using a geographic information system (GIS) or a contouring application such as Surfer.
  3. Create a centerline for the waterbody and define the grid spacing in the longitudinal (x) direction for each model branch.
  4. Draw polygons around each model segment and create a Volume-Area-Elevation curve for each segment.

  5. After choosing an appropriate vertical layer spacing, compute segment widths for each vertical layer using:

    \[B = \frac{V_{\text{layer}}}{\Delta x \cdot \Delta z}\]

    where \(V_{\text{layer}}\) is the volume in the layer, \(\Delta x\) is the segment length, and \(\Delta z\) is the layer height.

  6. Assemble all layer widths for each segment into a file compatible with the CE-QUAL-W2 bathymetry format.

Note

Cross-sections can also be used directly to compute segment widths at various elevations. This approach is appropriate when the cross-section is representative of the model segment.

docs.title: Step 3: Edit the Main Control File
docs.text:
The main control file, w2_con.csv, is the central file that describes how the model will run. This file is generated from the Excel macro workbook w2_conDeGray4.5.xlsm. Do not edit the CSV file directly. Instead, edit the parameters within the .xlsm workbook and produce the w2_con.csv file by pressing the output button on the corresponding tab.

Enable macros

The Excel .xlsm file must have macros enabled for the output buttons to work.

The control file specifies:

  • Simulation start and end times
  • Inflow and outflow locations
  • Input and output file names
  • Water quality kinetic parameters
  • Output file designations and content

The .xlsm workbook also contains additional sheets that serve as auxiliary control files for different processes, as described in Step 4.

docs.title: Step 4: Edit Auxiliary Input Files
docs.text:
If additional processes are to be included in the simulation, auxiliary input files are required. Templates for these files are included in the .xlsm workbook. The following table lists the auxiliary input files and their associated processes.

File Process w2_diagenesis.npt Sediment diagenesis w2_selective.npt Automatic port selection particle.csv Particle tracking w2_aerate.npt Aeration w2_envirp.npt Environmental performance w2_habitat.npt Habitat suitability constriction.npt Channel constrictions pH_buffering.npt pH buffering dynselevX.npt Dynamic selective withdrawal elevation dynpumpX.npt Dynamic pump operation dynpipe.npt Dynamic pipe flow w2_systdg.npt System Total Dissolved Gas (TDG) multiple_WB.npt Multiple waterbody coupling w2_Algae_Toxin.csv Algae toxin modeling

Output procedure for auxiliary files

Unlike the main control file (w2_con.csv), auxiliary input files require the user to first select the cells in the .xlsm workbook and then press the output button to write the file.

docs.title: Step 5: Run the Preprocessor
docs.text:
The preprocessor executable, preW2-4_64.exe, checks the control file, bathymetry file, and all boundary condition files for errors before running the full simulation.

  1. Double-click preW2-4_64.exe to launch the preprocessor.
  2. Review the preprocessor screen output.
  3. Examine the output files produced by the preprocessor:
File Description pre.opt Echo of input data and other diagnostic information pre.err Fatal error messages pre.wrn Warning messages

Resolve all errors before proceeding

Always review both pre.wrn and pre.err before running the model. Correct any errors reported in pre.err and rerun the preprocessor until no errors remain.

docs.title: Step 6: Run the W2 Model
docs.text: The model executable is w2_v4_64.exe. Double-click the executable to launch the simulation. The model displays a dialog box showing simulation progress and a dynamic animation of results during the run.

docs.title: Step 7: Evaluate Output Files
docs.text: CE-QUAL-W2 output files have either an .opt or .csv extension, depending on the output type specified by the user in the control file.

docs.title: Key Output Files
docs.text:
File Description snp.opt Snapshot file containing water surface elevations, velocities, temperatures, and constituent concentrations at user-specified intervals Time Series Result (TSR) files Time series output files suitable for plotting in Excel Spreadsheet files Additional output files in spreadsheet-compatible format Contour plot (CPL) output Contour plot output compatible with Tecplot 360 (www.tecplot.com) for animating results

The post-processor utility w2_post.exe can be used to generate animations and contour plots from model output.

Tip

Open snp.opt in a text editor for a quick review of model results. Use the TSR and spreadsheet output files for detailed analysis and comparison with observed data. For a complete description of all output file formats, see Part 3 of this manual.

docs.title: How to Use Batch Processing and the Command Line with CE-QUAL-W2
Overview
docs.text: The CE-QUAL-W2 model preprocessor and executable are command-line aware. Users can execute both programs from any directory and specify the default model directory as a command-line argument. This capability is particularly useful for linked models that run independently as separate model applications rather than as one large, combined model.

docs.title: Linked Model Workflow
docs.text:
Consider an example with two linked CE-QUAL-W2 models stored in separate directories:

  • c:\w2\LakeA: an upstream lake model
  • c:\w2\RiverBelowLakeA: a downstream river model that receives outflow from the lake

The general workflow for linked models is:

  1. Run the preprocessor for each model to verify input files.
  2. Run the upstream model first.
  3. Copy the upstream model's output files to serve as input files for the downstream model.
  4. Run the downstream model.

Batch files automate this process so that the entire sequence executes without manual intervention.

docs.title: Preprocessor Batch File
docs.text:
The following batch file (checkW2.bat) runs the preprocessor for both model directories in sequence:

prew2-v4_64.exe "c:\w2\LakeA"
prew2-v4_64.exe "c:\w2\RiverBelowLakeA"

When the preprocessor runs, it opens a dialog box displaying results. The dialog box must be closed manually before the next command in the batch file executes. This behavior is by design, allowing the user to review the preprocessor results for each model before proceeding to the next.

docs.title: Model Run Batch File
docs.text:
The following batch file (runW2.bat) runs both linked models and transfers the necessary output files between them:

w2_v4_64.exe "c:\w2\LakeA"
copy "c:\w2\LakeA\qwd.opt" "c:\w2\RiverBelowLakeA\qin.npt" /Y
copy "c:\w2\LakeA\twd.opt" "c:\w2\RiverBelowLakeA\tin.npt" /Y
copy "c:\w2\LakeA\cwd.opt" "c:\w2\RiverBelowLakeA\cin.npt" /Y
w2_v4_64.exe "c:\w2\RiverBelowLakeA"

This batch file performs the following steps in order:

  1. Run the upstream lake model (LakeA).
  2. Copy the withdrawal flow output (qwd.opt) to serve as the inflow file (qin.npt) for the downstream model.
  3. Copy the withdrawal temperature output (twd.opt) to serve as the inflow temperature file (tin.npt) for the downstream model.
  4. Copy the withdrawal constituent output (cwd.opt) to serve as the inflow constituent file (cin.npt) for the downstream model.
  5. Run the downstream river model (RiverBelowLakeA).

The /Y flag on each copy command suppresses the overwrite confirmation prompt, allowing the batch file to run without user interaction.

Quotation marks in file paths

Enclose directory paths in quotation marks to handle paths that contain spaces. This is standard practice for Windows batch files and prevents errors when directory or file names include spaces.

docs.title: Automatic Dialog Box Closure
docs.text:
By default, the CE-QUAL-W2 executable opens a dialog box that remains open after a model run completes. In a batch processing workflow, this requires the user to manually close each dialog box before the next command executes.

Set CLOSEC to ON for unattended batch runs

Set the CLOSEC parameter to ON in the control file (w2_con.npt) to automatically close the dialog box when the model run finishes. This allows batch files to proceed through multiple model runs without manual intervention. When CLOSEC is set to OFF (the default), the dialog box remains open after each run, which is useful for reviewing run status before continuing.

docs.title: Relative Directory Paths for Input and Output Files
Overview
docs.text:
By default, CE-QUAL-W2 expects all input and output files to reside in the same directory as the executable and the control file (w2_con.npt). For large projects with many waterbodies, branches, tributaries, and output files, a single directory becomes difficult to manage. Organize files into subdirectories to improve project clarity and simplify locating specific inputs or outputs.

CE-QUAL-W2 supports relative directory paths in the control file. Instead of placing every file in the model root directory, create subdirectories and reference them using relative path notation.

docs.title: Creating a Subdirectory Structure
docs.text:
Consider a model with its root directory at c:\w2\LakeA. A practical directory structure might include:

Directory Contents c:\w2\LakeA\ Executable, w2_con.npt, and other control files c:\w2\LakeA\Inflows\ Flow, temperature, and concentration input files for branch inflows, tributaries, and distributed tributaries c:\w2\LakeA\Inputs\ Bathymetry file, shading file, wind sheltering coefficient file c:\w2\LakeA\output_snp\ Snapshot output files c:\w2\LakeA\output_tsr\ Time series output files

Tip

Choose a naming convention that clearly distinguishes input directories from output directories. This prevents accidental overwriting and simplifies archiving of model results.

docs.title: Specifying Relative Paths in the Control File
docs.text: In w2_con.npt, use the .\ prefix to specify file paths relative to the directory containing the executable. The backslash (\) separates subdirectory names from filenames, following standard Windows path conventions.

docs.title: Input File Examples
docs.text:
To place the wind sheltering coefficient file and the shading file in the Inputs subdirectory:

WSC FILE...............................WSCFN...............................
      .\Inputs\wsc.npt
SHD FILE...............................SHDFN...............................
      .\Inputs\shade.npt

To place branch inflow files (flow, temperature, and concentration) in the Inflows subdirectory:

QIN FILE...............................QINFN...............................
BR1    .\Inflows\qP88_2012.npt
TIN FILE...............................TINFN...............................
BR1    .\Inflows\tin_P88_2012.npt
CIN FILE...............................CINFN...............................
BR1    .\Inflows\cP88_2012_updated.npt

docs.title: Output File Examples
docs.text:
To direct snapshot and time series outputs to their respective subdirectories:

SNP FILE...............................SNPFN...............................
WB 1    .\output_snp\snp_wb1.opt
TSR FILE...............................TSRFN...............................
      .\output_tsr\tsr.csv

Warning

The subdirectories must exist before running the model. CE-QUAL-W2 does not create directories automatically. If a specified subdirectory is missing, the model will fail when it attempts to open the file.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Create subdirectories under the model root directory to organize input and output files.
  2. In w2_con.npt, replace bare filenames with relative paths using the .\ prefix (e.g., .\Inflows\qP88_2012.npt).
  3. Verify that all referenced subdirectories exist before running the model.

Note

Relative paths are resolved from the working directory where the executable runs. If you launch the model from a different directory, such as via a batch file, set the working directory to the model root directory. See Batch Processing and Command Line for details on running models from batch scripts.

docs.title: Appendix A: Contributors to the Development of CE-QUAL-W2
docs.text:
The list of contributors to the release version of CE-QUAL-W2 is long. It is difficult to identify all individuals who have contributed to the model's development, so this list may only be partial.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) has been the primary developer of the CE-QUAL-W2 model. This development work was spearheaded by Tom Cole at ERDC, moving the model from Version 1 to Versions 2 and 3. His efforts to advance the use of the model cannot be overstated. The development work at Portland State University (PSU) is a continuation of that original development. The goals of this development are:

  1. To create a tool useful for improving water quality and managing waterbodies to meet their beneficial uses.
  2. To make that tool freely available.

docs.title: Major Contributors
docs.text:
The following individuals have made major contributions to CE-QUAL-W2 development:

  • Ed Buchak and John Edinger: Hydrodynamic code development and model support through Version 2.
  • Tom Cole: Spearheaded development of W2, developing Version 2 and working with S. Wells on Version 3. Worked to make W2 a workable model and helped countless individuals with early W2 applications. Started the W2 modeling workshop in the late 1990s. Primary author of two major user manuals.
  • Chris Berger: Developed the macrophyte model, integrated and revised the sediment diagenesis model, developed the pipe algorithm, and contributed to Versions 3.1 through 4.2.
  • Rob Annear: Developed the shading algorithm and contributed to many developments in Versions 3.5 through 3.7.
  • James Martin: Worked on Version 1 water quality algorithms and the user manual.
  • Ray Chapman: Developed coding for Ultimate QUICKEST and the foundation of turbulence algorithms updated and revised by Gould.
  • Stewart Rounds: Added the automatic port algorithm option (U.S. Geological Survey [USGS]), non-conservative alkalinity, many bug fixes, and excellent code suggestions such as refining multiple waterbody algorithms.
  • Annette Sullivan: Worked with Stewart Rounds on the automatic port algorithm option (USGS), non-conservative alkalinity, many bug fixes, and code suggestions.
  • Zhong Zhang: System total dissolved gas (SYSTDG) algorithm implementation, significant improvements to the sediment diagenesis model, and work on the mercury (Hg) model.

docs.text:

  • John Tobiason and Lillian Jeznach: Generic constituent photo-degradation.

docs.text: • ERDC 2026.02 (February 2026) -- Based on PSU V4.5

docs.title: CE-QUAL-W2 Version 2026.02
docs.text: Release Date: March 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: CE-QUAL-W2 Version 2026, developed by the Environmental Laboratory, U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is the first release under the new ERDC versioning system. It is based on Version 4.5, developed by Portland State University (PSU). ERDC Version 2026 includes recent Harmful Algal Bloom (HAB) simulation capabilities developed at ERDC as well as support for multiple operating systems. ERDC supports CE-QUAL-W2 on Windows, macOS, and Linux/HPC operating systems.

docs.title: Harmful Algal Bloom (HAB) Modules
docs.text:
Four new algorithms for simulating harmful algal bloom dynamics:

  • Nitrogen fixation: allows cyanobacteria groups to fix atmospheric nitrogen when dissolved inorganic nitrogen concentrations fall below a user-defined threshold.
  • Hypoxic algal mortality: applies enhanced mortality rates to algal groups when dissolved oxygen drops below a specified concentration.
  • Minimum algae concentration: prevents algal concentrations from falling below a user-specified minimum, representing persistent seed populations or benthic recruitment.
  • Mechanical removal: simulates physical removal of algal biomass from specified segments and layers, representing management interventions such as harvesting or skimming.

docs.title: Multi-Platform Support
docs.text:
• Compilation with gfortran (replacing Intel Fortran dependency).
  • Pre-compiled binaries for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), and Linux.
  • Compilation and execution scripts for DoD HPC systems.

docs.text: All features present in PSU V4.5 are included in ERDC V2026 unless noted otherwise in the documentation. ERDC-specific modifications are flagged throughout with the "ERDC Feature" annotation.

docs.title: Version Lineage
docs.text:
CE-QUAL-W2 has been developed collaboratively by the U.S. Army Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) and Portland State University (PSU). Since 2021, ERDC has maintained the official version for use on U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) projects.

This page documents the relationship between ERDC and PSU releases to ensure transparency and reproducibility for the user community.

docs.title: Versioning Convention
docs.text:
ERDC uses a YYYY.MM versioning scheme where YYYY is the release year and MM is the sequential release number within that year. This distinguishes ERDC releases from PSU's version numbering (V4.x, V5.x) and clearly identifies the provenance of each release.

Each ERDC release specifies its PSU base version, ensuring that users can identify which PSU features and formulations are included. ERDC-specific additions are documented in the corresponding release notes and flagged throughout this documentation with the ERDC Feature annotation.
